recap_lines: A vertex shader moves corners, and a fragment shader colours pixels.
Rasterization makes fragments, and a varying is blended across them.
A compile error can still leave the run's exit code at zero.
A uniform is set from code, and hint range does not clamp it.
A shader is the program, and a material is the shader plus its values.
Step switches hard at its edge, and smoothstep eases between two edges.
bookends.command: Quiz me on Godot shader terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms vertex shader, fragment shader, varying, uniform, hint range, clamp, material, shared material, step and smoothstep. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Newcomers often think the vertex shader colours the pixels. It does not. A vertex shader runs once per corner and decides where that corner lands. Colour is the fragment shader's job, once per pixel. Shaders are full of look-alike pairs like that one. This film goes through the terms, each one shown, so you can name the exact one.

beats.narration_text: A grid of small squares fills with colour. A Shader is a small program that runs on the graphics processor, many copies at once. Here one program runs three hundred eighty-four times, once per cell, and each run works out its colour from its own position. No run can look at another run's result. For example, the failure flash in the Walker game is a shader. The same few lines run for every pixel of Clawd, the player character.

beats.narration_text: Now the other two boxes are lit. Fixed-function means a step that is built in. You can set its options, but you cannot program it. The name comes from older graphics hardware, where every step worked like this. Here two of the four are built in, rasterization, and blending with the depth test. For example, choosing an additive blend for a fire sprite, so it brightens what is behind it, is picking an option, not writing code.

For example, when a platform sprite is drawn, rasterization works out which screen pixels it covers, before any fragment shader gives them a colour.

beats.narration_text: Every covered cell now has a blended colour. Interpolation, in the shader sense, means blending the corner values smoothly across the triangle's fragments. Each fragment takes a mix weighted by how near it is to each corner. The outlined cell has weights of zero point three two, zero point four four and zero point two three. For example, a sky drawn as one big rectangle, dark blue at the top corners and pale at the bottom ones, gets a smooth gradient from interpolation alone.
